title: Hierarchical SAEs: Explicitly Encoding Feature Hierarchies to Eliminate Absorption
description:
Problem: Feature absorption in SAEs arises because standard SAE training optimizes for sparsity without awareness of hierarchical feature relationships, causing parent features to become absorbed into their children. This undermines reliable detection of broad semantic concepts in LLM activations.

Proposed Method: We propose Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (H-SAEs), which explicitly model feature hierarchies during training. H-SAEs learn a two-level (extendable to multi-level) dictionary where parent features are structurally constrained to activate whenever any of their child features activate, implemented via a soft hierarchical regularization loss: L_hier = sum over parent-child pairs of max(0, child_activation - parent_activation). We automatically discover hierarchical groupings through iterative clustering of feature co-activation statistics from a pretrained baseline SAE, then use these as structural priors when training H-SAEs from scratch. The architecture adds lightweight gating connections between parent and child decoder directions to enforce the containment constraint.

Experiments: (1) Measure absorption rates using the metric from the anchor paper across baseline SAEs vs H-SAEs at matched sizes on GPT-2, Llama-3 8B, and Gemma-2 9B. (2) Evaluate reconstruction fidelity (L0/MSE tradeoffs). (3) Assess probe accuracy for hierarchical concepts (e.g., country→continent, token→POS category) at parent and child levels. (4) Human interpretability study rating feature coherence. We predict H-SAEs substantially reduce absorption while maintaining or improving reconstruction quality.

title: HierarchySAE: Explicitly Encoding Feature Hierarchies in Sparse Autoencoders to Mitigate Absorption
description: Problem: Feature absorption in SAEs arises because standard SAE training treats all features as independent, ignoring natural parent-child hierarchical relationships (e.g., 'math' subsuming 'algebra'). When sparsity is enforced, parent features get suppressed in favor of their children, making interpretability unreliable. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchySAE, which augments SAE training with an explicit hierarchical structure. During training, we (1) automatically discover feature hierarchies via post-hoc co-activation clustering across expanding SAE sizes, (2) encode these hierarchies as a learnable tree structure where parent feature activations are constrained to be >= the maximum child activation (soft relaxation via a penalty term), and (3) add a hierarchy-consistency loss that penalizes parent features firing below their child features. The sparsity penalty is applied only to leaf features, allowing parent features to remain active when any child is active. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on GPT-2 and Pythia-1.4B using the established absorption metric from the anchor paper, measuring absorption rates across feature hierarchies. We compare against standard TopK-SAEs and JumpReLU-SAEs at matched parameter counts. We run probing tasks (e.g., first-letter identification) to verify that parent features correctly fire in all expected contexts. We also measure reconstruction loss and interpretability scores via automated labeling to confirm no quality degradation.

title: Hierarchical SAEs: Explicitly Encoding Feature Hierarchies to Eliminate Absorption
description: Problem: Feature absorption in Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) arises because standard SAEs impose a flat decomposition on activation spaces, forcing a sparsity trade-off when features form natural hierarchies (e.g., 'letter' → 'vowel' → 'a'). Parent features get absorbed into children, making interpretation unreliable. Proposed Method: We introduce Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (H-SAEs), which explicitly represent features at multiple granularity levels using a tree-structured latent space. Each parent feature is constrained to activate as a superposition of its children via a learned soft partition, with a residual component capturing non-hierarchical variation. We enforce hierarchy through a differentiable tree-structured sparsity penalty that rewards parent activation only when no child fires, preventing absorption by construction. The hierarchy can be discovered automatically via agglomerative clustering over co-activation statistics during training. Planned Experiments: (1) Reproduce absorption metrics from the anchor paper on standard SAEs as baseline; (2) Train H-SAEs on GPT-2 and Pythia activations across multiple scales, measuring absorption rates using the anchor paper's metric; (3) Evaluate interpretability via automated labeling agreement (GPT-4 judging feature descriptions) and probe accuracy on linguistic feature hierarchies; (4) Ablate the hierarchical constraint to isolate its contribution to absorption reduction versus standard TopK/L1 SAEs.

title: HierarchySAE: Explicitly Encoding Feature Hierarchies in Sparse Autoencoders to Mitigate Absorption
description: Problem: Feature absorption in SAEs arises because standard SAE training treats all features independently, ignoring that natural language concepts form ontological hierarchies (e.g., 'math' → 'algebra' → 'linear equations'). When a parent feature's activation can be fully explained by child features, sparsity pressure suppresses the parent, causing absorption and breaking robustness of mechanistic interpretability pipelines. Proposed Method: We propose HierarchySAE, which augments standard SAE training with an explicit hierarchical regularization term. Using an automatically-induced feature hierarchy (via post-hoc clustering of learned SAE features across multiple scales), we add a 'hierarchical consistency loss' that penalizes cases where a parent feature fails to fire when any of its children fire. We further introduce a parent-reconstruction auxiliary objective ensuring parent features encode strictly more general information than their children, preventing redundancy-driven absorption. We also propose a modified activation function ('hierarchical ReLU') that allows parent features to remain active at reduced magnitude when child features are active. Experiments: We train HierarchySAE on GPT-2 and Llama-3-8B activations, measuring absorption rates using the metric from the anchor paper across hundreds of feature families. We evaluate downstream probing accuracy on hierarchical attribute tasks (country→continent, species→genus) and compare against baseline SAEs and TopK-SAEs, demonstrating significantly reduced absorption with maintained reconstruction quality.

title: Hierarchical SAEs: Exploiting Known Feature Hierarchies to Mitigate Absorption via Structured Sparsity Constraints
description:

Standard SAEs have no mechanism to encode or exploit known hierarchical relationships among features, making absorption an emergent failure mode.

Proposed Method: We introduce Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (H-SAEs), which augment the standard SAE training objective with a structured sparsity constraint derived from an explicit feature hierarchy. Concretely, we propose a 'hierarchical consistency loss' that penalizes cases where a child feature fires without its parent feature also activating proportionally. The hierarchy can be bootstrapped automatically by clustering SAE features learned at multiple scales (small and large SAEs trained sequentially), then constructing a parent-child graph via cosine similarity thresholds. The H-SAE is then trained end-to-end with this graph as a soft regularizer, preserving parent feature activation whenever descendants fire.

Experiments: (1) Compare absorption rates (using the metric from the anchor paper) between standard SAEs and H-SAEs across GPT-2 and Llama-3 layers. (2) Evaluate reconstruction fidelity, sparsity, and interpretability (automated LLM-grading of feature descriptions). (3) Ablate hierarchy construction methods (manual vs. automated clustering).
